memories.content: The user changed their schedule once in November 2024 because of their mother's hospital visit.
After seeing the reason for the schedule change written in a calendar invitation, the user asked for it to be removed.
The user was able to reschedule the appointment after providing only a new time, without a reason.
On a day the user traveled in their father's car, they photographed the parking location.
On the next visit, when the user did not take a photo, they walked one circuit of the parking garage while looking for the exit.
After hearing preparation items from their mother by phone, the user omitted two items.
After receiving the preparation items again by text, the user put all of them in their bag.
The user's mother does not want the reason for her visit disclosed in the user's external schedule.
Do not include the mother's reason for a visit when conveying the user's availability externally.
Some daily-life services may operate for shorter hours during the year-end holiday period.
The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains. The reference frame concerns schedule privacy, practical memory aids, preparation, and holiday service hours; the compared frame concerns food storage, shopping checks, recipe adjustment, collaborative cooking, and limits on preference inference. No cross-frame operational claim is shared or opposed.

relations.reason: These memories form one reference-only scheduling episode showing both the unwanted disclosure and that the reason was unnecessary for rescheduling.
relations.summary: A November 2024 schedule change initially disclosed the mother's hospital visit, after which the user requested removal of the reason and successfully rescheduled using only a new time.

relations.reason: These memories state the same reference-only privacy preference and its operational communication rule.
relations.summary: The mother's visit reason should not be disclosed when the user's availability is communicated externally.

relations.reason: These memories describe a connected reference-only sequence about using, then omitting, a visual parking aid.
relations.summary: The user photographed a parking location on one visit and, on the next visit without a photo, made a circuit of the garage while seeking the exit.

relations.reason: These memories form one reference-only contrast between spoken and written preparation instructions.
relations.summary: The user omitted preparation items received verbally but packed every item after receiving the information by text.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only caution about seasonal service availability.
relations.summary: Some daily-life services may have shorter operating hours during the year-end holiday period.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only storage-location fact.
relations.summary: The user stores prepared meals on the freezer's second shelf.

relations.reason: These memories form one compared-only contrast about using inventory information before shopping.
relations.summary: The user made a duplicate purchase without a list but avoided one after checking a refrigerator photo.

relations.reason: These memories describe one compared-only recipe-adjustment sequence and its observed meal outcome.
relations.summary: After leaving spicy stew unfinished, the user used half as much chili powder the next time and finished the meal.

relations.reason: These memories jointly describe one compared-only claim about advance division of collaborative cooking responsibilities.
relations.summary: Verbal-only task sequencing with the younger brother caused duplicated work, while explicitly splitting preparation and heat control finished cooking earlier and aligns with his preference for advance role division.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only constraint on drawing food-preference conclusions.
relations.summary: Food responses may be compared across several meals, but one unfinished item does not establish that the user dislikes an ingredient.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only qualification about frozen-food condition.
relations.summary: The condition of frozen prepared food may depend on packaging and storage duration.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only material covers freezer storage, shopping checks, recipe adjustment, cooking-role coordination, cautious food-preference inference, and frozen-food variability.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only material covers private scheduling reasons, parking and packing memory aids, and possible year-end service-hour reductions.
